recentItems.title: How the media manufactured consent for genocide: Assal Rad interview | The Listening Post
recentItems.description:
Assal Rad built a reputation on social media as the “headline fixer” for her work correcting journalistic sins at major news outlets.

The historian joins presenter Richard Gizbert to discuss her new book, Don’t Say Palestine: How the Media Manufactured Consent for Genocide.

In it, Rad traces the role the mainstream media played in normalising the dehumanisation of Palestinians and whitewashing Israel’s genocidal campaign in Gaza.

Contributor:
Assal Rad – Author, Don’t say Palestine: How the media manufactured consent for genocide.

recentItems.title: Israeli attacks kill at least eight Palestinians across Gaza despite ceasefire
recentItems.description:
Israeli forces have killed at least eight Palestinians in the latest attacks across Gaza, including an eight-year-old girl on her way to school and a three-year-old boy in a classroom at a school sheltering civilians. The Israeli military says it launched attacks on Hamas sites in the north after one of its vehicles struck an explosive device. Attacks have continued across Gaza despite a US-brokered ceasefire that took effect in October. The situation remains “extremely fragile”, with Israeli officials “signalling more military options” and the transition to the second phase of the ceasefire agreement remaining contentious. 

Al Jazeera's Tareq Abu Azzoum reports from Deir el-Balah, Gaza.

recentItems.title: Iran's new Hormuz zone could widen conflict, analyst warns
recentItems.description:
Iran's top security official says Tehran will introduce a new restricted zone around the Strait of Hormuz and parts of the Gulf, and announce a new maritime route agreed with Oman. Mohsen Rezaei said any ship entering the zone will be placed on Iran's sanctions list. Military defence analyst Alexandru Hudisteanu told Al Jazeera the Oman deal is "unlikely to change materially the situation" as long as shipping remains concerned about threats in the strait. He said Iran's restricted zone announcement is a "counter-tactic" to the US blockade that could extend its area of operations beyond the strait's confines. He described the current exchange as an "escalatory cycle" with an "intrinsic risk of going all to full-out war", although both sides still believe they can control it. Hudisteanu also said Iran may be developing missiles capable of striking US carrier groups, which would "complicate significantly US strategy".

recentItems.title: Kenya's HIV programmes falter after US funding cuts, patients suffer
recentItems.description:
Community health groups in Kisumu, Kenya, say US funding cuts have devastated HIV/AIDS support networks, forcing outreach programmes to scale back drastically. One group reported condom distribution falling from 30,000 to just 1,000 monthly, while home visits to vulnerable patients have stopped entirely. Kisumu's HIV prevalence remains four times Kenya's national average, a legacy of the epidemic's severe impact on lakeshore fishing communities since the 1980s. 
Antiretroviral medicines remain available at government clinics, but health officials warn that without restored funding, decades of progress against the virus could unravel, with the gravest consequences still ahead.

Al Jazeera's Malcolm Webb reports.

recentItems.title: At least 17 killed and 20 others injured in Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon
recentItems.description:
At least 17 people have been killed and 20 wounded in Israeli air strikes across southern Lebanon over the past 48 hours.
One strike hit a residential area in Deir al-Zahrani after Israel issued an evacuation order, while another struck Kfar Reman, killing at least nine people, including children and a two-month-old infant.
Israeli forces say they targeted sites linked to Hezbollah and accuse the group of launching armed drones at Israeli positions. 
The attacks have continued despite a US-brokered ceasefire framework between Israel and Lebanon, while residents who had returned home are again fleeing the area.
Israel says it will intensify attacks unless Hezbollah is disarmed across Lebanon, while Hezbollah says it is prepared to disarm south of the Litani River but not in the north.
A diplomatic process between Lebanon and Israel has stalled, with no date set for the next round of talks.

Al Jazeera's Zeina Khodr reports from Kfar Reman in southern Lebanon.
